rules_sent_back.instruction: When the description states that, while other activities are under way, a participant performs a further preparation step of its own (for example, readying an item in parallel with the work of others): Model that described step as its own task on a parallel branch that starts at the same split as the concurrent activities, and join it with those branches before the step that depends on all of them. Do not drop the step or fold it into another task.
rules_sent_back.situation: the description says that a participant prepares several pieces of information separately (one of them while another activity such as describing a problem is under way) and then sends them together in one message

rules_sent_back.instruction: When the description says an action requests something from an outside party or source, and a later step can only proceed once that party's arrival or delivery happens at an unspecified or uncertain time: Model the request as its own task. Model the arrival or delivery as a distinct intermediate catch event placed after the request task and before the step that depends on it. Do not merge the request and the arrival into one element, do not represent the wait as a task or as internal work of another activity, and do not omit the request task. If the request is made on a parallel branch, keep the catch event on the path that leads to the dependent step.
rules_sent_back.situation: the description says an action requests something from an outside party or source, and a later step can only proceed once that party's arrival or delivery happens at an unspecified or uncertain time
rules_sent_back.source: learned guideline (refines ACT-05), generalized from EXS-089

rules_sent_back.instruction: When the description states that after a scheduled appointment an external party arrives at an unspecified time, and that the visit may end without the goal achieved, so the next step depends on whether the goal was reached: Model the scheduling task, then an intermediate catch event for the arrival of the external party, placed directly after the scheduling task and before the activity performed on arrival. Model the activity performed on arrival as a task followed directly by an exclusive gateway with one conditional outgoing flow per stated result. Route the achieved result to the next step or the end event, and route the incomplete result back to the wait for the missing condition or to the earlier step that must be retried. Do not use an event-based gateway after the activity, because no event is awaited at that point; the result is produced by the activity itself.
rules_sent_back.situation: the description states that after a scheduled appointment an external party arrives at an unspecified time, and that the visit may end without the goal achieved, so the next step depends on whether the goal was reached

rules_sent_back.instruction: When The description says a party whose visit has already been arranged will arrive at an unpredictable time, and that on arrival the work may be left unfinished and must be taken up again on a later visit.: Model the arrival as an intermediate catch event placed after the arrangement task and before the work task. After the work task, place an exclusive gateway with one branch that continues when the work is completed and one branch that returns to the arrival catch event when the work is unfinished. Do not model the outcome as an event-based gateway, because the outcome is a data-based result of the work and not a race between events.
rules_sent_back.situation: The description says a party whose visit has already been arranged will arrive at an unpredictable time, and that on arrival the work may be left unfinished and must be taken up again on a later visit.
